show: You'll Hear It: Full Album Deep Dives with Jazz Musicians
titel: Waltz for Debby – Bill Evans Trio

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: Exploring the brilliance of the Bill Evans Trio's live album Waltz for Debby.
kurzfassung: Adam Maness and Peter Martin explore the Bill Evans Trio's iconic 1961 live album Waltz for Debby recorded at the Village Vanguard. They analyze the groundbreaking interplay between Evans, bassist Scott LaFaro, and drummer Paul Motian. The hosts also discuss individual tracks, the album's lasting influence, and share listener mail.
stichpunkte: Discussion of the Bill Evans Trio's classic 1961 live album Waltz for Debby
Recording took place on June 25, 1961, at the Village Vanguard in New York City
Tragic context of bassist Scott LaFaro dying in a car accident eleven days after the session
Analysis of the trio's conversational playing style and individual contributions
Detailed breakdown of tracks including My Foolish Heart, Waltz for Debby, and Detour Ahead
Exploration of various vocal and instrumental covers of the album's standards
Examination of the unique acoustic qualities and challenges of recording at the Village Vanguard
Listener mail segment featuring a review and instructions for submitting questions

kapitel.titel: My Foolish Heart and Trio Dynamics
Waltz for Debby and Cover Versions
Vanguard Acoustics and Scott LaFaro Legacy

clips.hook: Starting an album with a ballad takes guts.
clips.text: The hosts discuss how opening a record with a slow, introspective ballad rather than an upbeat track is a bold and emotionally raw artistic choice.

clips.hook: The only time Bill Evans played rooted voicings.
clips.text: A technical observation is made about a specific moment during a bass solo where the pianist plays foundational chord voicings underneath.

clips.hook: Subway rumbles and a wedge-shaped room.
clips.text: The physical characteristics of the famous jazz club are described, including its unusual geometry, low ceilings, and proximity to a subway line.

clips.hook: One a.m. jazz sets are a thing of the past.
clips.text: The speakers express disbelief at the idea of audiences attending late-night performances stretching into the early morning hours in New York City.

clips.hook: A surprisingly thin piano sound on a classic record.
clips.text: One host offers a candid critique regarding the acoustic quality of the piano instrument capture compared to the perfection of the other drums and bass.

beschreibung:
Waltz for Debby is the sound that all "boring coffeehouse jazz" tries to imitate, but none can replicate. Featuring Bill Evans on piano, Scott LaFaro on bass and Paul Motian on drums, this 1962 live album has become the template for every AI jazz playlist. And yet, it stands apart as one of the greatest jazz piano trio albums of all time. Pianists Adam Maness and Peter Martin listen to the full album, track-by-track, describing what they hear in the music that lends this album its undeniable humanity.
